steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The five fundamental British values: democracy (government by the people through elected representatives), rule of law (everyone is equal before the law and no one is above it), individual liberty (freedom of speech, thought, association and personal autonomy), mutual respect (valuing others regardless of background), and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: British identity: what does it mean to be British? Identity is complex and multi-layered - people can identify as British, English/Scottish/Welsh/Northern Irish, and with their ethnic or religious heritage simultaneously. The concept of Britishness has evolved: from empire and monarchy to multiculturalism and pluralism.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Multiculturalism: the UK is a diverse, multi-ethnic, multi-faith society. About 14% of the UK population was born abroad; over 300 languages are spoken in London alone. The Equality Act 2010 protects people from discrimination based on race, religion, gender, sexuality and other characteristics.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Community cohesion: different communities living together peacefully and with shared purpose. Challenges: segregation, prejudice, extremism. The Prevent strategy aims to counter radicalisation. Community cohesion is promoted through: interfaith dialogue, shared community events, anti-discrimination law, and citizenship education itself.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Describe the five fundamental British values and explain why they are important. | Q: Evaluate whether British identity can be defined in a diverse, multicultural society. | Q: Assess the role of the media in promoting or undermining British values.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: 5 British values: Democracy, Rule of Law, Individual Liberty, Mutual Respect, Tolerance. Remember: DRIMT. British identity = shared VALUES + legal CITIZENSHIP, not ethnicity or birth. Media = essential for democracy but needs regulation (Ofcom, IPSO) and critical engagement.
